title: George Baquet as the best clarinetist, funerals around 1910
summary: Barbarin recalls George Baquet moving mourners to tears at a funeral and names other clarinetists of the time.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: But later on in years, I mean, around about 1910, when I remember my father of the bands, I knew who was the best clarinet player at that time. Because they had George Bakke and Lores Atillo. Well, they had other clarinet players, but they didn't come up to those guys. I think George was the best. Because any time they played a funeral, I remember they played a funeral on, they had a funeral on St. Anthony, between St. Claude and Lores. And she was a saloon called Delio. These people have a shoe store right here on the hop in Claiborne, I can't think of their name. Well, it was right next door, at that time, those people were living there, had a little shoe place there. This was starting to sell shoes, you see? Heckman or something like that? Heckman, that's right, Heckman. Those Heckman people, that's right. And it was about two years away from then, this person, this fellow had died. And George was knowing, George Bakke was knowing to make, any time they played a funeral, and he picked up the clarinet. I mean, everybody had tears in their eyes in those days. That's right, George Bakke, he's a fine looking man. I used to think that he was a pretty man. I was small, you know, I thought he was pretty looking. He had a face like a girl, like a woman. But he could play. Oh, he could play. Gee whiz. I never heard nothing like him, no more after that.
On the street they played E flat?

E flat, yeah, he played the E flats. Now, Larenza Tio, I mean, young Larenza, I mean, he was a very good clarinetist. Charlie McCurtis, he was good. They had Alphonse P. Kool, and I'm talking about the guys that could read at that time. I can remember, they had, you know, Big Al Lover, he was around that time, but he was a musician with those guys. He played Ratty, you know, he was a ratty kind of player. Later on in the years, well, I mean, what, Basher and them fellas came up with. But that Basher, Sidney Basher, he was the most.
